free_tier.stated: 1 TB per Dataverse Collection allocation (2.5 TB for Harvard affiliates). Per-file 2.5 GB through UI/API; larger via the S3 direct-upload path. The 1 TB is enforced as a collection allocation, not a per-person cap: GET /api/dataverses/<alias>/storage/quota?showInherited=true returns {"Total quota allocation for this collection": 1099511627776} for ordinary collections, and one live collection returns 2748779069440 (2.5 TB).

retention.stated: | write-once: publishing is irreversible, no delete without support intervention, no embargo; 'Submit for Review' spam screen before publication; per-file 2.5 GB in the browser path; 1,000 files/dataset is the observed effectiveDatasetFileCountLimit; S3 direct upload is admin-enabled per install and is the only route past the 2.5 GB file cap.

egress.terms: Free anonymous access without login. Endpoint GET /api/access/datafile/<id> returns HTTP 303 to a signed S3 URL with 1-hour expiration, supporting Range requests.

record.tooling: REST native API (create dataset, add files, direct S3 upload), plus the official Python/CLI clients. dataset count 306,027 live. rclone has no native backend but the S3 direct-upload path accepts any S3 client.
record.chaining: Storage quota attaches to collections, which logged-in users can create as of June 2024. Each collection receives a 1 TiB allocation, and collections can be nested into hierarchical trees for sharding.
record.limits_note: write-once: publishing is irreversible, no delete without support intervention, no embargo; 'Submit for Review' spam screen before publication; per-file 2.5 GB in the browser path; 1,000 files/dataset is the observed effectiveDatasetFileCountLimit; S3 direct upload is admin-enabled per install and is the only route past the 2.5 GB file cap.
record.reliability_note: Anonymous downloads return signed S3 URLs with 1-hour expiration, requiring URL resolution per request. Quota API endpoints rate-limit rapid successive requests with HTTP 403.

free_tier.stated: 2.5 GB per file; 1 TB per Dataverse Collection for non-Harvard researchers (2.5 TB for Harvard affiliates). The 1 TB is real and stated by Harvard, but it is a service/support threshold, not a hard enforced cap. See limits.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Public file access returns 303 -> a presigned S3 URL (dvn-cloud-iqss.s3.amazonaws.com) valid 3600s; S3 honours Range requests. No egress pricing exists anywhere in the product. Probe: GET /api/access/datafile/11685194 -L -H 'Range: bytes=0-1023' -> 303 then HTTP 206, Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/21269528, Server: AmazonS3.

record.tooling: Native REST API v6.10.1 (live: GET /api/info/version -> {"version":"6.10.1"}); SWORD v2 deposit; OAI-PMH harvest; S3 direct-upload API for files >2.5 GB (docs: 'This option can handle files >300GB'). Python client pyDataverse; R package dataverse. No rclone backend, but a REST loop is trivial (~15 lines) and the platform is a well-documented Invenio-free Java stack.
record.chaining: Unlimited Dataverse Collections per account (Harvard: 9,755 collections / 306,011 datasets exist, anyone may create one). x 1 TB per collection. 20 collections = 20 TB in one account; 20 accounts = 400 TB. Also multiplies per dataset rather than per collection if the 1 TB is read as a guidance number, since no per-dataset quota is enforced on the root collection.

record.limits_note: Per-file 2.5 GB through the Harvard UI/API; larger files require the S3 direct-upload path, which Harvard has enabled (downloads already redirect to S3, so upload-redirect is configured). Dataset file-count cap observed live: effectiveDatasetFileCountLimit=1000 (12 used on the sampled dataset). No enforced collection quota: GET /api/dataverses/harvard/storage/quota?showInherited=true -> {"message":"No quota defined for this collection"}. Publishing is a 'Submit for Review' spam-check gate, not peer review.
record.reliability_note: Mature, 15+ year old service with DOI permanence and S3-backed bytes; the only soft failure mode is a curator rejecting a deposit at the review gate, and the storage-quota feature is flagged 'new and still experimental' upstream.
record.confidence_note: The quota endpoint answers were read on 2026-10-21. The record keeps reported because the per-file cap and the identity field were not measured. Was reported, now documented.
